knobs.note: no static default — the script computes it (${HARNESS:-/root/harness}). Read by bin/tmp-sweep.sh as ${HARNESS_ROOT:-${HARNESS:-/root/harness}}. A test seam for BH-5007's sweep; NOT settable from the control plane — it is a path a root lane uses, so only env/global.env on the box moves it.

Minutes since the NEWEST write anywhere inside a /tmp top-level entry before bin/tmp-sweep.sh may remove it. Protects the live scratch of a running job: an entry with any write inside it in this many minutes is kept. Each firing costs nothing; it only frees space. Not a whole number at or over 30 skips the sweep with a log line. BH-5007, BH-5608.
/tmp Use% strictly over which bin/tmp-sweep.sh raises tmp-high-<host> (warn, the batched digest) after its sweep; resolved when /tmp is back at or under it. BH-5007.
Seconds bin/tmp-sweep.sh may spend reading the newest mtime inside one /tmp entry; an entry whose age is not read in time is kept and counted skipped_unreadable. BH-5007.
Total seconds for one bin/tmp-sweep.sh run; entries past it are left for the next run and counted left=. Not box-housekeeping's TMP_SWEEP_DEADLINE_S (disk-clean lane). BH-5007.

The hand-made stopgap cron file bin/tmp-sweep.sh removes after a real sweep when its only line is the BH-5007 stopgap. A test seam; NOT settable from the control plane — it is a path a root lane deletes, so only env/global.env on the box moves it.

no static default — the script computes it ($HARNESS_ROOT/state/claims). The live job claims dir bin/tmp-sweep.sh reads: a claim line naming a path under a /tmp entry keeps that entry. A test seam for BH-5608; NOT settable from the control plane — it is a path a root lane uses, so only env/global.env on the box moves it.

Test seam gate: when this is 1 and TMP_SWEEP_ROOT is unset, bin/tmp-sweep.sh skips the sweep with a log line, so a suite never sweeps the real /tmp (the test harness sets it). Never set on a box, and NOT settable from the control plane. BH-5608.
